alternativesRejected: Splitting the repository toolchain/scaffold and the core wire-type package into two separate plans — rejected because an empty scaffold is not independently verifiable, and the core types are small enough that combining them keeps the plan within a comfortable milestone count
Folding the servant HTTP surface into the core package — rejected so the core package stays dependency-light, allowing the hasql package and future non-servant consumers to avoid pulling in servant

A single monolithic ExecPlan covering all functionality — rejected because it spans five distinct functional concerns, would run well over five milestones, and would serialize the servant and hasql streams that are otherwise parallelizable
Adding a validation migration of one mls-service-v2 endpoint to prove the library against a real consumer — explicitly descoped by the user, who scoped the initiative to the library only
summary: The initiative was decomposed along package boundaries because those boundaries coincide with the functional and dependency boundaries of the system: wire format, HTTP surface, database engine, verification, and documentation. Each resulting stream (EP-1 through EP-5) produces an independently verifiable behavior — a test suite or observable artifact — rather than an arbitrary slice of work. EP-1 comes first because it establishes both the repository toolchain (nix flake, cabal.project, formatter, Justfile) and the core wire types that every other package imports, so nothing downstream can start without it. The two middle streams — EP-2 (servant surface) and EP-3 (hasql engine) — depend only on EP-1's core types and not on each other, so they were deliberately kept independent to allow parallel implementation in either order. EP-4 (conformance suite) was split out from EP-3 even though it primarily tests EP-3, because the conformance walker is itself a shipped public artifact with its own API surface and design constraints (it must stay usable outside the repo, independent of any specific hasql Session execution strategy), and because the adversarial correctness tests it contains are central enough to the library's core guarantee to warrant their own milestone structure. EP-5 (guides and release readiness) comes last and soft-depends on everything else, since it must demonstrate real, compiling code against the finished APIs.
